subject: Geography
description: Major Indian lakes — Wular, Dal, Pangong Tso, Chilika, Loktak, Vembanad, Sambhar, Pulicat — type, location, ecological significance.

questions.stem: WULAR LAKE, the largest freshwater lake in India, is in which region?
questions.explanation: WULAR LAKE — INDIA'S LARGEST FRESHWATER LAKE; located in BANDIPORA district, KASHMIR VALLEY (J&K). Area: ~30-260 sq km (varies seasonally — monsoons swell it). Source: JHELUM RIVER flows through it; major regulator of Jhelum's flow. KEY FEATURES: high biodiversity — fish (carp, schizothorax), waterfowl (migratory birds in winter), aquatic plants (lotus, water chestnut). Locally important: ~50,000 people depend on Wular for fishing, boating, water-chestnut harvesting. CONSERVATION: RAMSAR site since 1990; threatened by encroachment, pollution, willow plantation (introduced by British, choked native vegetation). RAMSAR CONVENTION: 1971 international treaty for wetland conservation; INDIA has 80+ Ramsar sites (2024). KEY INDIAN LAKES (memorize): (1) WULAR — J&K (largest fresh). (2) DAL LAKE — Srinagar (famous houseboats, shikara rides). (3) PANGONG TSO — Ladakh (saltwater, China border). (4) TSOMORIRI — Ladakh (saltwater high altitude). (5) NAINITAL — Uttarakhand. (6) BHIMTAL, NAUKUCHIATAL — Uttarakhand. (7) CHILIKA — Odisha (largest brackish, INDIA's largest lake by area). (8) PULICAT — TN/AP (2nd largest brackish). (9) VEMBANAD — Kerala (longest, 96 km). (10) LOKTAK — Manipur (floating phumdis). (11) SAMBHAR — Rajasthan (largest saline). PYQ FREQUENCY: Wular-Kashmir in SSC GA, UPSC, NDA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: CHILIKA LAKE, the largest BRACKISH-water lake in INDIA, is in which state?
questions.explanation: CHILIKA LAKE — INDIA'S LARGEST coastal LAGOON / BRACKISH-water lake; located in ODISHA (Puri, Khurda, Ganjam districts), connected to BAY OF BENGAL by a narrow channel. Area: ~1,100 sq km (avg); summer ~1,100 sq km, monsoon ~1,165 sq km. ECOSYSTEM: BRACKISH (mix of fresh river water + sea water); supports unique biodiversity. SIGNIFICANCE: (1) RAMSAR SITE (1981) — INDIA'S FIRST Ramsar wetland. (2) HOSTS ~1 MILLION migratory birds in winter from Central Asia, Mongolia, Siberia (largest wintering grounds for migratory water birds in India). Birds include flamingos, cranes, herons, ducks, sandpipers. (3) IRRAWADDY DOLPHIN — endangered species; ~150-200 in Chilika (one of largest populations). (4) FISHING industry: ~150,000 fishermen depend on it; produces ~13,000 tonnes/year. (5) Biodiversity: ~700 species of plants/animals. INSTITUTIONS: Chilika Development Authority (CDA, 1992) — manages conservation. PROBLEMS: SILTATION, decreased connection to sea, eutrophication. RECENT: in 2000, a NEW MOUTH was opened into the sea — improved salinity, fish stocks, ecology. INDIA'S LARGEST LAKE BY AREA: CHILIKA (1,100+ sq km) — beats freshwater Wular. WULAR LAKE is largest FRESHWATER lake; Chilika is largest BRACKISH and largest by total area. PYQ FREQUENCY: Chilika in UPSC, SSC, NDA 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: LOKTAK LAKE, famous for unique floating PHUMDIS (vegetation islands), is in:
questions.explanation: LOKTAK LAKE — MANIPUR's largest natural lake (~287 sq km); unique for its FLOATING ISLANDS called PHUMDIS — heterogeneous mass of vegetation, soil, organic matter that floats on water surface; some big enough to support people. WORLD'S ONLY FLOATING NATIONAL PARK: KEIBUL LAMJAO NATIONAL PARK on the southern part of Loktak — protects the SANGAI (brow-antlered deer, Cervus eldii eldii) — Manipur's STATE ANIMAL; critically endangered (~250 left as of 2024). RAMSAR SITE since 1990. ECOLOGY: phumdis SUSTAIN about 200 species of aquatic plants, ~100 species of birds, ~400 species of animals. SOURCE: drained by KHUGA, NAMBUL, and other rivers; outlet is MANIPUR RIVER. CONCERNS: shrinking lake area, pollution from Imphal (state capital, ~50 km away), invasive water hyacinth, sedimentation. ITHAI BARRAGE (1983) — built for hydropower (LOKTAK PROJECT, 105 MW); altered water levels, contributing to ecological problems. CULTURAL: Loktak is central to Manipuri culture; festivals, songs, traditional fishing methods. NEAR ATTRACTIONS: KANGLA Fort (Imphal), Imphal War Cemetery, KEIBUL LAMJAO. NORTH-EAST INDIA OVERVIEW: 7 sister states (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura) + Sikkim. PYQ FREQUENCY: Loktak-Manipur in UPSC, SSC, NDA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: VEMBANAD LAKE, INDIA's longest lake (96 km), is in:
questions.explanation: VEMBANAD LAKE — INDIA's LONGEST lake (~96 km); area ~2,033 sq km when including all backwaters; located in KERALA (Alappuzha, Ernakulam, Kottayam districts). PART of the famous KERALA BACKWATERS — interconnected lagoons, channels, lakes. NAMED differently in different stretches: 'Vembanad' (Kottayam region), 'Punnamada Lake' (Alappuzha), 'Kochi Lake' (Ernakulam, near Kochi). UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE — backwaters not, but a Ramsar site since 2002. TOURISM: HOUSEBOATS ('kettuvallam' — 'kettu' = tied, 'vallam' = boat) — converted from cargo boats; iconic backwater experience; ~2-day cruises popular with foreign + domestic tourists. NEHRU TROPHY BOAT RACE held annually on Punnamada Lake (Alappuzha) — 100+ row boats compete; massive cultural event since 1952; 2024 winner: NADUBHAGOM CHUNDAN. ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES: pollution (industrial + sewage from Kochi), encroachment, reduced freshwater flow due to Thanneermukkom barrier. KEY: Thanneermukkom Salt Water Barrier (1976) — reduced salinity inflow but altered ecology. ECONOMIC: rice farming on POLDERS (reclaimed wetlands), fishing, prawns, mussels, coir industry, tourism. KERALA-WATERWAY-FACTS: 41 west-flowing rivers in Kerala drain into Arabian Sea via these backwaters. PYQ FREQUENCY: Vembanad-Kerala in SSC, UPSC GA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: SAMBHAR LAKE, the largest INLAND SALT lake of INDIA, is in:
questions.explanation: SAMBHAR SALT LAKE — INDIA's LARGEST INLAND SALT LAKE; located in JAIPUR & NAGAUR districts of RAJASTHAN, ~80 km W of Jaipur. Area: ~190-230 sq km (varies seasonally). HISTORICAL: source of SALT for centuries — mentioned in Mahabharata, given as DOWRY at Maratha-Rajput marriage 1730 between Marwar (Rajasthan) and Maratha empire. SALT PRODUCTION: ~9% of India's total salt comes from Sambhar (~200,000 tonnes/year); via solar evaporation. UNIQUE FEATURE: ~3 m DEEPER salt content than ocean; salinity 7-8% (vs ocean 3.5%). HABITAT: Greater FLAMINGOS gather here in thousands during monsoon — beautiful pink-water spectacle (water turns pink from algae blooms in salt-rich conditions). Other migratory birds: pelicans, cranes, ducks. RAMSAR SITE since 1990. AREA: average 19 km × 4 km, irregular shape. RECENT (2019): mass bird-die-off (~25,000+ birds) due to AVIAN BOTULISM linked to climate change (longer-stagnant water). RECOVERY ongoing. RAJASTHAN's WATER BODIES: SAMBHAR, PUSHKAR (sacred lake, Pushkar town), JAISAMAND (Udaipur, largest artificial lake), PICHOLA + FATEH SAGAR (Udaipur), ANA SAGAR (Ajmer). RAJASTHAN largest state by area; semi-arid; lakes are critical for water + ecology. PYQ FREQUENCY: Sambhar-salt-Rajasthan in SSC, UPSC, NDA 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: PANGONG TSO LAKE, situated at high altitude in Ladakh, has its border with which country?
questions.explanation: PANGONG TSO ('PANGONG LAKE' in Tibetan; 'tso' = lake) — high-altitude (~4,250 m / 13,900 ft) endorheic (no outflow) saline lake in EASTERN LADAKH. ~134 km long, ~5 km wide; ~700 sq km total area. SHARED: ~40% in INDIA (Ladakh, Indo-Tibetan border) + ~60% in CHINA (Tibet Autonomous Region) — runs ALONG THE LAC (Line of Actual Control). LAC: India-China de facto border (not formally agreed); origin of multiple military standoffs. CONFLICT: 2020 LADAKH STANDOFF — major Indo-China tensions; included clashes at Pangong Tso's NORTH BANK (Finger 4-8 area); resolved partially by 2021 disengagement, fully by Oct 2024 patrol agreement. STRATEGIC: northern bank features 'fingers' (mountain spurs) numbered 1-8 from west to east; India claims up to Finger 8, China up to Finger 4 — disputed area between fingers 4-8. UNIQUE FEATURE: water turns BLUE/GREEN/TURQUOISE depending on light + clouds; CINEMATIC fame from '3 IDIOTS' (2009 movie's climax filmed here at Pangong). FREEZES in winter (water saline but cold enough to freeze): solid ice from Nov-March. SPECIES: brown-headed gulls, Brahminy ducks; few fish (high salinity). ALTITUDE EFFECTS: oxygen ~60% of sea level; visitors warned about altitude sickness. PYQ FREQUENCY: Pangong-LAC in UPSC, SSC current affairs 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: DAL LAKE, the famous tourist lake of SRINAGAR, is fed primarily by which water source?
questions.explanation: DAL LAKE — second-largest lake of Jammu & Kashmir; ~18 sq km; located in SRINAGAR. Sources: SPRINGS + MOUNTAIN STREAMS (Telbal Nallah, etc.) carrying SNOW-MELT from surrounding HIMALAYAN PEAKS (Mughal Garden hills, Shankaracharya Hill, Hari Parbat). FAMOUS FOR: (1) SHIKARAS — wooden gondolas; tourists ride. (2) HOUSEBOATS — opulent floating accommodations (a heritage from British era). (3) FLOATING GARDENS — vegetable-growing on rafts (locally called 'rad'). (4) MUGHAL GARDENS surrounding — Shalimar Bagh (Jahangir, 1619), Nishat Bagh (Nur Jahan's brother Asaf Khan, 1633), Chashma Shahi (Shah Jahan, 1632). (5) Centerpiece of Kashmir Valley tourism. POLLUTION: severely polluted by 1990s-2000s; sewage, encroachments, weeds (water-chestnut, lotus, pollutants). RESTORATION: Lakes & Waterways Development Authority (LAWDA, formed 1997) leading restoration. RECENT IMPROVEMENTS visible. DAL VS WULAR: DAL is in Srinagar, smaller, urban-touristic; WULAR is N. of Srinagar, much larger, less touristic, more biodiverse. KASHMIR VALLEY GEOGRAPHY: bowl-shaped, surrounded by Pir Panjal (S) and Greater Himalayas (N); JHELUM RIVER drains it. CULTURAL: 'Switzerland of India'. KEY POEMS: Allama Iqbal called Kashmir 'Heaven on Earth'. PYQ FREQUENCY: Dal Lake in SSC GA, UPSC tourism 1× per cycle.
